claim: Every plane embedding of the exact one-node order A_0 is polynomially equivalent to Y^2=X^3+X^2.
inspection: Internal primary-source reading and rendered-page inspection.

sources.title: Complex algebraic plane curves via their links at infinity
sources.author: Walter D. Neumann

inspected.content: Definitions of regularity at infinity and good polynomials; reduced knot fibre implies good.
Section 8 low-genus classification uses algebraic automorphisms of the ambient plane; genus-one table is cubic Weierstrass.
Last paragraph applies the table to a C-normalized curve with one node, yielding the standard nodal cubic.

applicability: Its finite normalization is A^1, with one point at infinity.
Its sole singularity is an ordinary node.
The singular fibre is not assumed regular; the good-polynomial lemma supplies regularity at infinity.
sources.source_correction: The last paragraph's assertion that c1*(X^3-Y^2+X^2)+c2 has only one singular fibre is false: the two values are c2 and c2+4*c1/27. The normal form of the given nodal fibre follows instead from its double-root cubic factorization.

inspected.content: Corrected definition of good polynomial; corrected Lemma 7.1 applies to a reduced fibre with a knot at infinity.
Proof of Lemma 7.1 uses Suzuki's connectedness at infinity, fibreability of the iterated torus knot, and corrected Theorem 6.1.

excluded_import: The conditional classification in Borodzik-Zoladek's later parametric-lines paper is not used.
